title: Making Embedded Systems: Design Patterns for Great Software
reason: Readable design and interrupt introduction alongside processor-specific manuals.

inspection.method: Local edition title/front matter and bounded PDF passage extraction; publisher metadata search
inspection.scope: Physical pp. 195–201; interrupt entry narrative, priority and nesting discussion
inspection.limits: Examples use STM32F103xx and generalize across processors. The fault/NMI narrative must be checked against Arm exception terminology; this book is not the F439 register oracle.

title: Test-Driven Development for Embedded C
access: Held locally; commercial book with publisher sample
reason: Gives a concrete host/evaluation-board/target testing progression and explicit dual-target risks.
locators: Stage 3—Run Unit Tests in an Eval Board
Stage 4—Run Unit Tests in the Target Hardware
Stage 5—Run Acceptance Tests in the Target

inspection.method: Local title/front matter and bounded PDF passage inspection; publisher metadata search
inspection.scope: Printed pp. 108–111; stages, compatibility checks and target acceptance
inspection.limits: Host tests and simulator runs do not establish actual peripheral behavior. Historical tooling references require current commands. This inspection supports the strategy passages, not all mock-driver chapters.

title: Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms
reason: Distinguishes summation algorithms, rounding error and ill-conditioned relative error; supports correctness requirements before optimization.

inspection.method: Local edition front matter and bounded PDF passages; author and publisher metadata search
inspection.scope: Printed pp. 80–85; recursive/pairwise/compensated summation and qualitative limitations
inspection.limits: Text extraction damages equations. Exact bounds need visual inspection before formula-level teaching. Compensated summation does not guarantee small relative error for severely cancelling sums.

title: Cortex-M4 Devices Generic User Guide
reason: Processor-level memory ordering, exception and fault semantics for the Cortex-M4 track.
locators: 2.2.2 Memory system ordering of memory accesses
2.4.3 Fault status registers and fault address registers

inspection.method: Official PDF capture with SHA-256 and bounded passage extraction
inspection.scope: Printed pp. 2-13–2-15 and 2-30–2-31, plus front matter Authoring addendum inspected printed pp.2-24–2-28: priority convention/grouping and actual basic/extended frame and EXC_RETURN descriptions/table.
inspection.limits: Generic core document; optional features and device integration require ST evidence. Publication year is not inferred from copyright or identifier. Read barrier instruction definitions before using the overview as a complete ordering specification.

title: Procedure Call Standard for the Arm Architecture
reason: Specifies register preservation, parameter passing and stack alignment for C/assembly boundaries.
locators: 6.2.1.2 Stack constraints at a public interface

inspection.method: Tagged official text passage inspection
inspection.scope: Core/VFP preservation, SP word alignment, public-interface double-word alignment and parameter-passing sections
inspection.limits: Select the actual ABI variant and floating-point options used by the toolchain; this document does not choose a board memory map or linker layout.

title: STM32F405/415, STM32F407/417, STM32F427/437 and STM32F429/439 advanced Arm-based 32-bit MCUs
access: Public English ST manual captured from ST Japan
reason: Defines memory reachability, boot mapping, clock and sleep controls, GPIO/DMA contracts, representative serial/ADC/timer behavior and watchdog operation for F439.
locators: 13.6 Conversion on external trigger and trigger polarity
28.3.3 Configuring the SPI in master mode

inspection.method: ST Japan English PDF capture supplied by chief librarian; independently extracted and inspected bounded passages
inspection.scope: Printed pp. 68–69, 129–131, 156–157, 163–164, 277–278, 309–310, 393, 613–614, 711–712, 843, 849 (master-mode opening), 879–880, 973–974, 1010–1012. Actual functional text/register contracts read; heading lookup used only to locate these passages. Authoring addendum: printed p.394 single conversion; p.400 sampling/trigger; pp.849–852 I2C start/address, transmitter and single-byte receiver closing; pp.885–886 and 888–890 SPI master configuration/full-duplex procedure; p.977 character reception; p.981 baud-generation text/formula.
inspection.limits: Inspected Rev21; newer Rev22 delta uninspected. F439 RCC is chapter6, not earlier-family chapter7. Additional authoring inspection supports bounded 7-bit I2C transmit/single-byte receive and full-duplex SPI sequencing; optimized I2C multibyte/NACK timing and full error chapters remain outside scope. ADC sampling/trigger/single conversion are inspected, but analog electrical accuracy and Stop/Standby recipes are not. Physical timings, package pins and device electrical conditions need DS/board evidence and measurement.

title: STM32F437xx STM32F439xx datasheet
reason: Identifies the actual device family and memory/bus integration that generic Cortex-M descriptions omit.

inspection.method: Official PDF web passage inspection
inspection.scope: Front features and printed pp. 22–23 memory/bus sections
inspection.limits: Family-wide 'up to' feature summaries are not part-specific guarantees. Exact package pins, alternate functions, electrical conditions and target operating point need their own datasheet passages when an exercise selects them.

title: STM32 Nucleo-144 boards (MB1137)
access: Public English ST manual from ST Japan; captured by chief librarian
reason: Connects F439ZI software bring-up to actual board clock sources and USART3 virtual COM port solder bridges.

inspection.method: Selected captured English PDF independently hashed and bounded passages inspected
inspection.scope: Front applicability includes NUCLEO-F439ZI; printed pp. 25–26 clock and USART configuration
inspection.limits: Inspected Rev 8, not current Rev 11. Board revision, actual solder bridges and clock population must be recorded on physical hardware; described defaults are not a measurement of the learner's board.

title: STM32F427/437 and STM32F429/439 device errata
reason: Makes silicon limitations and required ordering workarounds part of firmware review.
locators: 2.1.3 Store immediate overlapping exception return operation might vector to incorrect interrupt
2.2.7 Delay after an RCC peripheral clock enabling

inspection.method: Official PDF web passage inspection
inspection.scope: Revision applicability summary and printed pp. 8–11 descriptions, conditions and workarounds
inspection.limits: An erratum applies only under its listed conditions and revision applicability. No physical board revision was read. DSB and dummy-read remedies must not be generalized to unrelated devices.

title: Arm MPS2 and MPS3 boards
edition: Master documentation; footer reported QEMU 11.1.50 at inspection
reason: Defines the scope of the mps2-an386 Cortex-M4 emulator and its differences from the FPGA hardware.
locators: Differences between QEMU and real hardware:

inspection.method: Complete short official board documentation passage inspection
inspection.scope: Cortex-M4 AN386 image, low-memory remapping limitation and Ethernet-model difference
inspection.limits: A moving development manual, not the installed emulator version. MPS2 is an Arm FPGA platform; it does not model STM32F439 peripheral registers, physical pin behavior, silicon errata or calibrated physical timing.

title: CMSIS-Core (Cortex-M): Startup File startup_<device>.c
reason: Shows vector-table, weak-handler and C runtime entry responsibilities and the adaptation obligations of a startup file.

inspection.method: Official versioned HTML passage inspection
inspection.scope: Startup description, vector table and Reset_Handler example
inspection.limits: Generic template contains adaptation TODOs and Armv8-M stack-limit/sealing operations; it must not be copied verbatim to Cortex-M4. Device startup and linker/runtime initialization must be inspected for the selected compiler.

title: Scheduling Algorithms for Multiprogramming in a Hard-Real-Time Environment
access: Original paper inspected in university-hosted scan
reason: Foundational source for fixed-priority critical instants and utilization-bound reasoning with explicit task-model assumptions.

inspection.method: Original paper scan parsed and bounded passages inspected; SWE metadata used only as retrieval lead
inspection.scope: Printed pp. 47–49; assumptions A1–A5 and Theorem 1 critical-instant argument
inspection.limits: Single-processor periodic independent tasks with period-related deadlines and constant/max execution costs. Does not by itself establish schedulability with blocking, jitter, arbitrary deadlines, DMA contention, or a real RTOS port.

title: FreeRTOS Kernel GCC ARM_CM4F port
reason: Exposes real Cortex-M4F interrupt priority assertions, context-save operations and timer configuration rather than relying on a generic RTOS explanation.

inspection.method: Tagged raw source passage inspection; official documentation search used as a lead
inspection.scope: Scheduler interrupt setup, PendSV register/FPU save and restore, FromISR priority validation, SysTick setup
inspection.limits: Source symbols are locators because this is source code. A particular GCC CM4F port is not a generic RTOS guarantee; no port build or timing experiment was run. Assert checks and configuration assumptions remain essential.

title: An Axiomatic Basis for Computer Programming
access: Original paper inspected in university-hosted scan
reason: Introduces preconditions, postconditions and assignment reasoning while explicitly discussing machine arithmetic choices.

inspection.method: Downloaded original scan; physical pp. 1–2 rendered and visually inspected
inspection.scope: Printed pp. 576–577; arithmetic axioms, overflow interpretations and program-triple notation
inspection.limits: A small illustrative language and historical formalism, not modern C semantics. Signed overflow, aliasing, memory safety and termination need current C/tool evidence. Remaining paper pages were not visually inspected.

title: CBMC training: What is loop unwinding?
reason: Explains loop-bound completeness checks and the off-by-one relationship between loop body traversals and guard tests.

inspection.method: Complete bounded official practitioner training page inspected; CBMC official release news checked
inspection.scope: Bounds, unwinding assertions and counting semantics; official CBMC version 6 changed defaults
inspection.limits: Training examples do not select a release or prove a hardware environment. Pin tool version, check defaults and report assumptions, reachability and every unwinding result. The old CPROVER manual routes returned navigation only.

title: WP Plug-in Manual
reason: Contract proof instructions connect Hoare reasoning to concrete proof obligations and memory/arithmetic model choices.

inspection.method: Official current PDF captured, hashed and bounded passages inspected
inspection.scope: Printed pp. 6–12; swap tutorial, missing/skipped runtime-error guards, model trade-offs and limitations
inspection.limits: Proof is conditional on contracts, runtime-error obligations and models. Tutorial reports skipped unaligned-pointer/function-pointer guards. The Real Model explicitly does not establish C/IEEE floating-point correctness. Selected passages only; no solver execution.

title: The Eva plug-in
reason: Provides a distinct static-analysis method with over-approximated value sets and alarms, suited to a bounded portable driver/application core.
locators: 1.2 Run-time errors and the absence thereof
5.5.1 The C standard and its practice

inspection.method: Official current PDF captured, hashed and bounded passages inspected
inspection.scope: Printed pp. 9–11 and 48; alarm interpretation and analysis-model limitations
inspection.limits: False alarms can result from approximation. Soundness is relative to the specified context and supported semantics. Current manual states asynchronous interrupts are not directly modeled; do not claim full firmware proof from sequential analysis.

title: ANSI/ISO C Specification Language
reason: Defines the specification language and separates mathematical logical integers from executable C machine arithmetic.

inspection.method: Official versioned PDF captured and inspected; release index verified
inspection.scope: Annotation categories and printed pp. 16–17 typing and integer logic
inspection.limits: Logical arithmetic has no machine overflow by default. Language expressiveness does not imply every clause is supported by each plug-in; WP limitations must accompany assignments.

title: What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic
edition: Oracle edited reprint of the 1991 ACM Computing Surveys paper
reason: Readable original treatment of rounding, ulps, cancellation and conditions that matter before numeric transformations.

inspection.method: Oracle reprint actual passages inspected; SWE lead independently checked
inspection.scope: Introductory rounding and cancellation sections
inspection.limits: An edited historical reprint, not the current IEEE 754 specification or a guarantee about the selected compiler flags. Formula-heavy material needs original rendering when used quantitatively.

title: Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization
reason: Provides version-specific evidence for optimization levels, aliasing assumptions, vectorization and floating-point semantic changes.

inspection.method: Versioned official HTML passages inspected
inspection.scope: Optimization-level flag sets, vector cost model and fast-math description Authoring addendum: actual LTO compile/link consistency, plugin/version constraints and profile-use generation/mismatch paragraphs inspected.
inspection.limits: The reference version is deliberately fixed; installed compiler identity and target-dependent behavior require separate evidence. Enabling fast-math changes admissible numeric semantics and needs a documented error/exception contract.

title: Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures
access: Original article inspected in university-hosted copy; author laboratory bibliography checked
reason: Makes optimization a measured bound-and-bottleneck argument, relating operation rate and traffic across a specified memory boundary.

inspection.method: Original article web PDF passages inspected; author laboratory publication metadata verified
inspection.scope: Printed pp. 66–68 and 74; operational intensity, empirical bandwidth and model limits
inspection.limits: Original examples are multicore floating-point kernels with DRAM traffic. It is a reasoning model, not a universal prediction or proof of Cortex-M4 latency, WCET or energy. State the measured memory boundary and ceilings.

title: Cache-timing attacks on AES
reason: Concrete primary case study showing how secret-indexed memory operations affect timing and leak information.

inspection.method: Author-hosted PDF captured, hashed and bounded passages inspected
inspection.scope: Physical pp. 1–4; reported attack, terminology, target platform and explicit preliminary-version note
inspection.limits: Historical Pentium III/OpenSSL experiment; it neither proves a Cortex-M4 leakage mechanism nor supplies production cryptography. The paper itself labels this a preliminary version. Use only a controlled educational threat model.

title: The Definitive Guide to ARM Cortex-M3 and Cortex-M4 Processors
access: Commercial book; publisher metadata/table of contents inspected
reason: Promising processor tutorial lead with edition-specific chapter coverage; requires full passage access before assignment.

inspection.method: Publisher bibliographic and table-of-contents inspection only
inspection.scope: Third-edition identity and chapters on exceptions, faults, FPU and MPU
inspection.limits: Not assignable: no actual chapter passage inspected. Local title/author retrieval did not find an ordinary held payload. SWE node mixed date ranges and was not accepted as edition evidence.

title: SEI CERT C Coding Standard: Rules for Developing Safe, Reliable, and Secure Systems

inspection.method: Official download redirect and registration-page inspection only
inspection.scope: Edition identity and access conditions
inspection.limits: Not assignable: old direct PDF URL returned HTML registration form; current rule pages returned gateway errors. No registration form was submitted. Indexed rule snippets were not treated as passage verification.

title: Clang SSE2 intrinsic header, selected definitions

inspection.method: Actual bounded function/option text inspected; complete capture hashed privately
inspection.scope: Comments and actual definitions at lines 2090–2116, 3447–3463 and 3901–3917.
inspection.limits: These functions specify four-lane modulo integer addition and full 16-byte unaligned access; unaligned access still requires the complete valid extent. Intrinsic header/source version is fixed, installed compiler is not verified. No other intrinsic or ISA dispatch mechanism was inspected.

title: GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts
reason: Authoring addendum supplies an exact tool/intrinsic contract absent from the earlier bibliography.

inspection.scope: Coverage/condition instrumentation, selected sanitizer detection/linking/incompatibility/recovery paragraphs, hardening aggregate and stack-protector definitions. Profile-generation compile/link and runtime-data paragraphs also inspected.
inspection.limits: Selected options only, not every instrumentation feature. Flag availability and effective dependencies vary with installed compiler/target. GNU/Linux hardening aggregate is not a bare-metal recipe; instrumentation changes resource/timing behavior.

inspection.limits: Does not verify installed GCC internals or OS support for arbitrary AVX state. Teaching core specialization uses SSE2 on an identified supported x86 host; AVX/ifunc expansion requires additional OS-state and loader research.
